relevance_note: Familial case report of Blau syndrome with individual-level detail on two siblings carrying a NOD2 variant: "Sequencing of the NOD2 gene revealed a novel heterozygous mutation, c.1439 A>G (p.His480Arg) in exon 4, in both patients."
method_note: Read the paper in full and built the JSON with a short Python script from values chosen by hand; spans checked verbatim by script. Six individuals: the two genotyped siblings (Case 1 index, Case 2), three affected paternal relatives described in relation to them (father, paternal aunt, aunt's daughter; untested: 'DNA samples of other family members were unavailable'), and one previously published Korean case (ref 6) given an individual-level variant (R334W). Relatives get no variant rows because they were not genotyped; the authors' inference of paternal inheritance from the pedigree was not used (inheritance 'not reported'). Previously published cardiovascular manifestations linked to C495Y (ref 14) and G481D (ref 15) were not given rows: the text names mutation-feature associations, not identifiable persons. Ages at diagnosis (8 and 10) come from 'their diagnosis was delayed until the age of 8 and 10, respectively', matched to the siblings' stated ages. Case 1 aortic stenosis 'suggestive of midaortic dysplastic syndrome' and 'vascular involvements' were recorded as observed features, but the vasculitis checklist item was left 'not reported' because the paper never calls it arteritis or aortitis; Case 1 upper-limb blood pressure 126/60 mmHg is not called hypertension, so systemic hypertension is 'not reported' for her. 'The siblings did not show significant visual disturbances or limitation of joint movements' was recorded as excluded phenotypic_features rows for both siblings (named group), but the checklist item 'visual impairment or blindness' was left 'not reported' because 'significant' is narrower than any visual impairment. Case 2 'CT of chest and abdomen were normal' and 'echocardiogram was normal' are whole-investigation normal findings, recorded in the paper's terms ('abnormal CT of chest and abdomen', 'abnormal echocardiogram' excluded) without excluding hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, lung disease or pericarditis. Case 2 arthritis checklist marked observed from 'pain in multiple lower limb joints ... indicating arthritic changes' (authors' interpretation). 'The brother had more prominent joint involvement than the sister' was not used to mark joint involvement in Case 1. Subcutaneous nodules (Case 2) were not mapped to erythema nodosum or panniculitis. No contradictions found.
